qualifiers.toolTip: Concurrency inside PanDDA. Changes how fast it runs and how fast it hits the memory ceiling; it does not lower peak memory.

PanDDA's --max_shell_datasets, default 60. It is also the floor below which PanDDA takes comparator datasets REGARDLESS of resolution, and a dataset is processed at the worst resolution among its comparators. So on a campaign with fewer datasets than this, every dataset is a comparator and one bad crystal sets the resolution for the whole run. Set it below the number of good datasets to make the resolution filter bite.

PanDDA's --max_events_per_dataset, default 3. It returns this many events per dataset, highest-scoring first, and autobuilds only those; the rest are discarded. Three is low for a campaign whose crystals carry recurring non-ligand density: a real binder ranked fourth is never reported or built, which looks like a site with no hits rather than a truncated list. Raising it costs build time roughly in proportion.

qualifiers.guiLabel: Minimum datasets to characterise a ground state
qualifiers.toolTip: PanDDA's --min_characterisation_datasets, default 25. A dataset with fewer comparators than this is skipped without analysis. Lower it only for a small test set; below about 25 the ground-state statistics are poor.
Where Ray spills (RAY_TMPDIR). Needs tens of GB on a fast local disk. Empty: a ray_scratch directory inside this job.
Which registered program run target runs PanDDA (dispatch mode). Empty: the only one this deployment registers.
Explicit path to pandda2.analyse. Empty: the PANDDA2_EXECUTABLE preference, then PATH, then the one CCP4 ships.
